title: Operator Runbook Stitchboard — compact UI for staged rollouts, emergency snapshots, and cost-delta inspection
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Operators and SREs need a compact, single-pane experience in Redwood Console to reason about staged rollouts (canary/A-B/traffic splits) during live incidents. Current rollout screens are too spread across tabs: metrics, traffic controls, cost projections, and runbook steps are siloed.

Goal: Prototype an 'Operator Runbook Stitchboard' — a condensed, action-oriented canvas that stitches together live metrics, simulated traffic sliders, emergency snapshot (instant rollback) controls, and a cost-delta inspector. The UI should make emergency decisions faster while surfacing cost and quality trade-offs.

Key user stories:
- As an on-call operator, I want to see a single view where I can: inspect health signals, simulate shifting traffic, preview cost delta before committing changes, and trigger an emergency snapshot rollback with a single confirmation flow.
- As a product owner, I want the runbook panel to display the rationale for each step (e.g., metric thresholds and historical context) so I can approve rollouts quickly.
- As an engineer, I want keyboard-first shortcuts and a compact mobile-safe fallback for paging scenarios.
acceptance_criteria: Single-pane stitchboard mockup with sections for: Live Metrics Pulseboard, Traffic Simulation Slider, Cost Delta Inspector, and Emergency Snapshot CTA
Interactive prototype demonstrates: simulated traffic reallocation, live cost projection updates, and a two-step emergency rollback flow
Design includes accessibility checks: color contrast for health badges, focus order for keyboard navigation, and ARIA labels for simulation controls
Copy and microcopy for runbook steps and risk explanations written and reviewed by PM
Handoff-ready Figma file with component tokens and an assets page for developers
design_notes: Stitchboard is a horizontally stacked layout on wide screens; collapses to tabbed vertical layers on narrow widths
Pulseboard: use sparkline + delta pill + small histogram for distribution of latency and error rates across variants
Traffic Simulation Slider: allow granular editing (percent text input) and 'Fast-snap' buttons for +10%/-10% increments; show projected QPS and estimated token cost
Cost Delta Inspector: lightweight model that shows incremental per-minute cost change, 1h/6h/24h projected burn, and annotations for billing region differences
Emergency Snapshot: two-stage modal — Stage 1 lock (describe impact), Stage 2 confirm with typed key + optional alert escalation checkbox
Safety nets: automated validate step before applying simulated changes (conflict check with active autoscale policies), suggested automatic reversion timer option
Telemetry hooks: event names for 'simulate_change', 'commit_change', 'trigger_snapshot', 'cancel_snapshot' to instrument later
Visual language: compact chips for variant names, muted separators, and a strong danger affordance for rollback actions
Interaction idea: 'Explain rollback' tooltip that summarizes top 3 signals (e.g., error spike, latency regression, cost overshoot) with links to traces/dashboards
